_comment: One-shot historical backfill sources. This file is the ONLY place endpoint and variable names live, so correcting them does not mean touching code. Nothing here has been verified against the live API -- use `backfill_history.py --dry-run` to print exact URLs and curl one before committing to a full run.

_roles.feature: Safe to use as a model input. As-issued forecast: what the model predicted BEFORE the target hour.
_roles.verification: Actuals / verification series ONLY. Must never enter the feature set. See history/README.md.

previous_runs_ifs_hres.description: ECMWF IFS HRES deterministic, as issued. The day-ahead feature series.
previous_runs_ifs_hres._unverified: Variable suffix `_previous_day1` (the run issued one day before the target hour) and the 2024-01-01 floor are both unconfirmed from this environment. Confirm with --dry-run before a full run.
previous_runs_ifs_hres._limited_variables_warning: The Previous Runs API is documented as covering deterministic models with a LIMITED variable set. shortwave_radiation and wind_speed_100m in particular may not be available here. Run with --limit 5 first: a rejected variable should surface as a 400 on the first call rather than as 155 bad files.
previous_runs_ifs_hres._note: Model id `ecmwf_ifs025` here is HRES deterministic on the previous-runs host. The daily capture uses the same id on the ensemble host for ENS. Same string, different product.

historical_forecast_actuals.description: LEAKAGE RISK IF USED AS A FEATURE. Open-Meteo stitches each run's first few hours into a continuous series, which makes this close to analysis -- effectively observations, not a lower-fidelity forecast. Actuals and verification only.
historical_forecast_actuals._note: Runs from the CAISO window start (2023-05-01), earlier than the 2024-01-01 modeling window, because the extra 2023 months are useful for descriptive work.

ensemble_mean.description: Ensemble mean/spread from the archive, via the *_ensemble_mean_* model variants. Same host and path as the daily capture; the model id is what selects mean/spread instead of members.
_confirmed_models: VERIFIED 2026-07-26 against the live ensemble API. Three ensemble_mean model ids confirmed to return all 8 variables (four fields + _spread each): dwd_icon_eps_ensemble_mean_seamless (DWD ICON), ncep_gefs025_ensemble_mean (GFS/GEFS), ecmwf_ifs025_ensemble_mean (ECMWF IFS). Note the naming is not uniform: the DWD id carries a _seamless suffix, the GFS and ECMWF ids do NOT. Invalid ids return HTTP 400 'Cannot initialize MultiDomains from invalid String value', which is the cheap way to probe new candidates.
ensemble_mean._archive_access: The archive is reached with past_days rather than start_date/end_date, so this source makes ONE call per location+model covering the whole window back to start_date, written as archive.json.gz.
ensemble_mean._past_days_limit: VERIFIED 2026-07-26 against the live API: the ensemble host caps past_days at 93 ('Allowed range 0 to 93'). start_date must stay within ~93 days of today or every call 400s. Set to 2026-04-25 for this reason -- an earlier floor (2026-03-01 was tried) is rejected. This is a hard upstream limit: mean/spread older than the window is not retrievable here, so run this source periodically to keep extending coverage forward rather than expecting a single deep backfill.
ensemble_mean._seam_warning: DO NOT concatenate this with the daily members capture into one continuous feature. Archive mean/spread and mean/spread computed from captured members are different statistics -- different generating process, member counts and derivation. The provenance field above is recorded into every manifest entry so the seam stays visible downstream. See history/README.md.

_rejected_previous_runs_for_ensembles._why_this_stub_exists: So the option is not re-derived from scratch later. Using the Previous Runs API to get as-issued ENSEMBLE history does not work: per Open-Meteo's author that API covers deterministic models only, with a limited variable set, because the ensemble equivalent would be roughly 2 TB for barely three months. Ensemble mean/spread history comes from the ensemble_mean source above instead. Do not build against this.
